title: OSHA Confined Space Rescue Checklist (29 CFR 1926.1211)
subtitle: Use before each construction permit space entry to confirm rescue arrangements and retrieval equipment are in place.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
If an item is marked Defect, do not allow entry until it is corrected, and record what was done.
Manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Rescue service selection, briefing and SDS
items: Employer can show the prospective rescuer's ability to respond to a summons in a timely manner was assessed against the identified hazards
Employer can show the service's proficiency with rescue tasks and equipment was assessed for this permit space or type of space
Selected team can reach victims within a time frame appropriate for the hazards identified
Selected team is equipped for and proficient in the rescue services needed
Selected team has agreed to tell the employer immediately if it becomes unavailable
Each rescue team or service has been told the hazards it may face when called to this site
Selected team has had access to every permit space from which rescue may be needed, to plan and practice
SDS or similar written information for substances kept at the worksite can be made available to the medical facility treating an exposed entrant

sections.title: Employee rescuers: PPE, training and practice
items: Designated rescuers have received all equipment and training without paying for it
Each designated rescuer has the PPE needed to conduct permit space rescues safely
Each designated rescuer has been trained and is proficient in using that PPE
Each designated rescuer has been trained in their assigned rescue duties
Each designated rescuer has completed training and established proficiency as an authorized entrant under 1926.1207 and 1926.1208
Each designated rescuer has been trained in basic first aid and CPR
At least one team member with current basic first aid and CPR certification is available during the entry
Rescuers have done a simulated rescue within the past 12 months, or properly performed a real rescue in that period in the same or a similar permit space
Practice used the actual space or one simulating its opening size, configuration and accessibility, removing a dummy, manikin or person

sections.title: Non-entry rescue and retrieval systems
items: Non-entry rescue is used, or there is a stated reason that retrieval equipment would increase overall entry risk or not contribute to rescue
An entry rescue service is designated where non-entry rescue was not selected
Where non-entry rescue is selected, a retrieval system or method is used each time an authorized entrant enters
Before entry, the entry employer has confirmed emergency assistance would be available if non-entry rescue fails
Each authorized entrant wears a chest or full body harness
Retrieval line is attached at the center of the back near shoulder level, above the head, or at another point shown to give a profile small enough for removal
If wristlets or anklets are used, employer can demonstrate a harness is infeasible or more hazardous and wristlets or anklets are the safest, most effective option
Other end of the retrieval line is attached to a mechanical device or fixed point outside the space so rescue can start immediately
Mechanical device for deep vertical spaces
A mechanical retrieval device is available at vertical type permit spaces more than 5 feet (1.52 meters) deep
No retrieval lines likely to tangle with other entrants' lines and none that will not work in the space's internal configuration

references: 29 CFR 1926.1211: Rescue and emergency services (Part 1926 Subpart AA, Confined Spaces in Construction)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, text as of 2026-11-09
